prompt.context: Your client is a large pharmaceutical company, LifeVac Corp., specializing in vaccines. As part of its strategy to expand into emerging markets, the company is considering applying for a vaccine protocol program in Brazil. The protocols are government managed programs designed to vaccinate infants against prevalent childhood diseases. Companies can only apply for one vaccine protocol. If LifeVac is chosen, it would have exclusive rights to provide vaccines to the government for a five-year period. However, as a prerequisite to applying, the Brazilian government requires all applicants to build a manufacturing plant in the country.
prompt.question: You have been hired to assess whether or not LifeVac should apply for a vaccination protocol, and if so which vaccine it should apply with.

clarifying_info.q: What vaccines does LifeVac have available for this program?
clarifying_info.a: LifeVac has three vaccines under consideration: Vaccine 1, Vaccine 2, and Vaccine 3.

clarifying_info.q: What are the financials for each vaccine?
clarifying_info.a: Vaccine 1: plant cost $45M, unit sale price $20, profit margin 75%. Vaccine 2: plant cost $30M, unit sale price $15, profit margin 80%. Vaccine 3: plant cost $25M, unit sale price $10, profit margin 90%.

clarifying_info.q: What happens if the application is not accepted?
clarifying_info.a: LifeVac will lose its initial plant investment entirely.

clarifying_info.q: What is the population of Brazil and relevant demographic data?
clarifying_info.a: Estimated population: 200M; birth rate: 20 per 1,000; vaccination rate: 75%. Vaccines are all one-time vaccinations for infants only.

clarifying_info.q: Can the plant be used for multiple vaccines?
clarifying_info.a: No, the manufacturing plant can only be used for manufacturing one vaccine.

clarifying_info.q: Can vaccines manufactured in Brazil be exported?
clarifying_info.a: No. Sufficient capacity already exists at plants in other countries, so vaccines manufactured in Brazil will not be shipped overseas. However, there is scope for further expansion in Latin America if LifeVac proceeds.

clarifying_info.q: What is the probability of acceptance for each vaccine?
clarifying_info.a: The probability of acceptance can vary by vaccine, but LifeVac does not have any information on the probability for each vaccine.

framework: Market sizing: estimate the addressable infant vaccination market in Brazil
Revenue and cost analysis: calculate the profitability of each vaccine if the application is accepted
Risk/probability analysis: determine the break-even acceptance probability for each vaccine using expected value
Expected value analysis: compare vaccines on the basis of minimum required acceptance probability to be viable
Strategy to gauge or increase probability of acceptance (government engagement, competitive intelligence)
Recommendation: select the vaccine that best balances profitability and acceptance probability risk

questions.prompt: Size the market: how many infants will be vaccinated annually in Brazil?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply population by birth rate to get annual births, then apply the vaccination rate. 200M x (20/1,000) = 4M births/year x 75% vaccination rate = 3M vaccinated infants per year.

math.setup: Population x Birth Rate x Vaccination Rate = annual market size

questions.prompt: Calculate the 5-year profit (net of plant investment) for each vaccine, assuming the application is accepted.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply margin to sale price to get profit per unit, multiply by annual market size and 5 years, then subtract the plant investment. Vaccine 1 yields the highest profit at $180M.

math.setup: (Unit price x Profit margin x Annual market x 5 years) - Plant investment
steps: Vaccine 3: $10 x 90% = $9/unit; $9 x 3M = $27M/yr; $27M x 5 = $135M gross; $135M - $25M = $110M net

questions.prompt: Given that the probability of acceptance is unknown and varies by vaccine, what is the minimum acceptance probability needed for each vaccine to have positive expected value?
questions.guidance: Set expected value to zero: (probability x gross revenue) - plant investment = 0, so probability = plant investment / gross revenue. Vaccine 2 requires the lowest minimum probability (16.7%), making it the least risky bet on acceptance. A strong candidate transitions to this analysis after learning probabilities vary by vaccine.

math.setup: Break-even probability = Plant investment / Gross 5-year revenue
math.answer: Vaccine 1: 20%, Vaccine 2: 16.7%, Vaccine 3: 18.5% — Vaccine 2 requires the lowest acceptance probability to be viable

brainstorming.prompt: What actions could LifeVac take to gauge or increase the probability of having its vaccine application accepted by the Brazilian government?

categories.name: Competition
ideas: Gauge competitors' interest in applying for the same vaccine slots
Explore partnership opportunities with local or regional players

categories.name: Government
ideas: Meet with government officials to build relationships and understand priorities
Analyze past applicants selected to identify patterns and preferences
Understand the political structure and forecast potential changes that could affect the decision

recommendation: LifeVac Corp. should build a plant in Brazil and apply for the protocol for Vaccine 1: it is the most profitable option, generating $180M in net profit over the 5-year period
LifeVac only requires a 20% acceptance probability for Vaccine 1 to be expected value positive, which is a reasonable threshold
Entering Brazil also positions the firm for further Latin American expansion
Alternatively, a more risk-averse client could favor Vaccine 2, which requires only a 16.7% acceptance probability (the lowest of the three) while still generating $150M net profit
risks: If the application is not accepted, the entire plant investment is lost (sunk cost)
Acceptance probabilities are unknown; actual probability may be below the break-even threshold
Political or regulatory changes in Brazil could affect the protocol program
The plant can only produce one vaccine, limiting operational flexibility
next_steps: Engage government officials and analyze past accepted applications to better estimate acceptance probabilities
Conduct competitive intelligence to understand which vaccines rivals may apply for
Perform deeper competitive analysis for long-term profitability of each vaccine in the Brazilian and Latin American markets
Develop a contingency plan for the plant investment if the application is rejected
